summary: Any array position can change the longest consecutive run, so a correct algorithm must inspect all n values in the worst case. The hash-set start scan performs linear total work under expected constant-time hashing.

optimality.argument: Consider an array containing only zeros. If an algorithm leaves any position unread, changing that value to one changes the longest consecutive sequence length from one to two while preserving all inspected values. Exact computation therefore requires Omega(n) inspections in the worst case. Set construction examines each input once, and the disjoint-run argument bounds all expected-constant-time membership probes by O(n), giving O(n) expected time.

replacement_checks.evidence: On an all-zero array, any unseen value can be changed to one and alter the answer, forcing inspection of all n positions.
Each distinct value is inserted once, checked once as a possible start, and advanced through only as part of its unique maximal run, assuming expected constant-time hashing.
The source-fidelity-verified examples cover isolated values, one long run, and duplicates; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
